text: Most people read a price the way they read a sentence: from the left, and only until they have enough. A seat price of $18 is read as “eighteen” long before the reader notices the word “seat”, so a plan that names its unit next to the number is well-known at a glance, and it wins over a cheaper plan that needs a second look.
Tiered plans ask for a decision first. The reader must place the team in a tier before the number means anything, and many leave the page at that step.

items.text: Show one price first, the one most teams pay.
Name the unit next to the number.
Put the tiers below, for the teams that need them.
